chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Sinan, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, from Abdul A'la ibn Ayn, who said:

He said: I was informed that Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) disliked two types of sales: 'Atkh khudh' (drop and take) without turning over (the goods to check them), and buying what has not been seen.

key_terms.اطْرَحْ وَ خُذْ: Drop and take (a specific type of sale where goods are thrown and taken without inspection)

ai.seo_question: What are the two types of sales disliked by Imam al-Baqir (AS) in commercial transactions?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi, transmitted through the chain of Yunus ibn Ya'qub, reflects the Imami juristic emphasis on minimizing uncertainty (gharar) in commercial contracts. It specifically critiques the 'Atkh Khudh' method—dropping goods for immediate pickup without inspection—and the sale of unseen items, aligning with the Shia scholarly tradition that prioritizes transparency and mutual consent to prevent dispute.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Sinan, from Yunus, from Ibn Sinan, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub, from Abdul Al A’ala Bin Ayn who said,

‘It has emerged from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> that he<sup>asws</sup> disliked selling the dropped (goods) taken upon without be turned around (checked for any damage), and buying what has not been seen’.
en.sarwar: 20. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn Sinan from Yunus ibn Ya’qub from ‘Abd al-‘A’la’ ibn ‘A‘yan who has said the following: “

I was told about abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, that he disliked two kinds of transactions: ‘Drop the merchandise without turning its other side and receive payment’, and ‘buying merchandise without seeing’.”
